function.name: rql-mutate
function.description:
Change the live Unity Editor scene with an RQL query whose last stage is set or call. All-or-nothing: every target and value is checked before anything is written; a failure changes nothing. Undoable in the Editor (Ctrl+Z). Changed assets, scenes and the open prefab are saved to disk automatically; an untitled scene needs SaveAs(path). dry_run=true returns the receipt ($ref, member, old, new) without changing anything. Do exactly the change requested; a read-only member fails with readonly-member instead of being approximated.
  set path = expr, ...   assign members (paths may go through structs: set transform.position.y = transform.position.y + 1)
  call Method(args)      invoke a method the tools expose
Examples:
  objects | where name == "Player" | set transform.position = "(0, 1, 0)"
  objects | get components | where $ is Light | set intensity = intensity * 2, color = "#ffcc88"
  objects | where tag == "Enemy" | set active = false
  unity.asset("Assets/Mats/Red.mat") | set properties["_Color"] = "(1, 0, 0, 1)"
  objects | where name == "Spawner" | set targets = append(targets, ref("GameObject#1234"))
Create / add / remove (call; the receipt's result column holds the new object's $ref for follow-up queries):
  editor | call CreateGameObject("Props")                                   new root GameObject
  editor | call CreateGameObject("Crate", ref("GameObject#1234"), "Cube")    child of a parent, optional primitive
  objects | where name == "Crate" | call AddComponent("Rigidbody")           add a component by type name
  objects | where name == "Old" | call Destroy()                             remove a GameObject (components: get components | where $ is X | call Destroy())
  objects | where name == "Lamp" | set transform.parent = ref("GameObject#1234")   reparent (keeps the world position)
  objects | where name == "Crate" | call Duplicate()                          copy next to it (returns the copy)
Scenes, prefabs, assets, Editor state:
  editor | call OpenScene("Assets/Scenes/Level.unity")          editor | call NewScene("Assets/Scenes/New.unity")
  scenes | where path == "" | call SaveAs("Assets/Scenes/New.unity")   scenes | where name == "Level" | call SetActive()
  editor | call InstantiatePrefab("Assets/Prefabs/Enemy.prefab", ref("GameObject#1234"), "(0, 0, 5)")
  objects | where name == "Crate" | call SaveAsPrefab("Assets/Prefabs/Crate.prefab")
  editor | call OpenPrefab("Assets/Prefabs/Enemy.prefab")  then  prefab | recurse children | …  then  editor | call ClosePrefab()
  editor | call CreateMaterial("Assets/Mats/Glow.mat")        editor | call MoveAsset("Assets/A.mat", "Assets/Mats/A.mat")
  editor | set selection = [ref("GameObject#1234")]         editor | set isPlaying = true
Object literals build values: set settings = {speed: 2, "$type": "FastSettings"}. At most 20 targets per call.

Query part: the RQL of rql-query (full guide in its description). Sources: objects, roots, scenes, selection, prefab, console, shaders, componentTypes, editor; unity.assets("t:Material"), unity.asset(path), unity.find("Name"), ref("Light#1234"). Stages: where, select, sort, first N, get <path>, recurse children. Operators: == != < > and or not, contains, starts-with, $ is Light. Paths a.b.c, list[0], map["key"]. Vectors/colors as "(1, 2, 3)" or "#ff8800"; enums as strings.

query.description: RQL query ending with a set or call stage, e.g. objects | where name == "Player" | set active = false

dry_run.description: true = preview the receipt without changing anything

function.name: rql-query
function.description:
Run a read-only RQL query against the live Unity Editor scene and return compact rows. One precise query beats many exploratory calls. Changes need rql-mutate.

RQL: source | stage | stage ...
Sources: objects (every GameObject in the loaded scenes, inactive included), roots, scenes, selection, prefab (the prefab open in prefab editing mode), console (Editor log entries), shaders, componentTypes, editor (Editor state and operations). Assets: unity.assets("t:Material") or unity.assets("t:Prefab", "Assets/Enemies"), unity.asset("Assets/Mats/Red.mat"). ref("Light#1234") resolves a $ref; unity.find("Player") or unity.find("Level/Pillar_1") a GameObject by unique name or path.
Stages:
  where <predicate>                  filter
  select a b.c alias=(expr)          project columns (wrap computed expressions in parentheses)
  sort <expr> [desc], ...            stable sort
  first N | skip N | count
  get <path>                         replace each item by a member (lists are flattened)
  recurse children [max-depth=N] [include-self=false]   walk the hierarchy (input items included by default)
  distinct [expr] | group-by expr | sum expr | min expr | max expr | avg expr
Expressions: == != < <= > >= and or not + - * / %; contains, starts-with, ends-with (case-insensitive); matches "regex"; x in [a, b]; x is null; x is not null; $ is Light (includes subclasses); has(member). Literals: numbers, "strings", true/false/null, lists [a, b], objects {x: 1, y: 2}.
Paths: a.b.c, list[0], map["key"]; .member on a list maps over its elements. List methods: .any(pred) .all(pred) .count([pred]) .sum(e) .min(e) .max(e) .first([pred]); inside them bare names refer to the element, falling back to the outer item.
Meta: $ (current item), $ref (stable id such as Light#1234), $type, $path, $index, $depth. Enums compare to strings (type == "Spot"); == on strings is case-sensitive.
Unity: GameObject has components (list), children (list), active, name, tag, layer, transform (position, localPosition, eulerAngles, localScale, parent). Component members are the C# members (public + [SerializeField]); find them via objects | get components | where $ is Light. Vectors/colors print as (x, y, z); write "(1, 2, 3)", [1, 2, 3] or {x: 1, y: 2, z: 3}; colors also "#ff8800". Material shader properties: properties["_Color"]. Destroyed objects read as null (missing references: where target == null). Navigate with paths or get; select only projects output columns.
Results come back as compact rows (header line, then col|col). Long results are truncated — refine with where/first or use count. Unknown members produce warnings with suggestions; rql-schema(type) lists a type's members.

Examples:
  objects | where name contains "Enemy" and active | select $ref name transform.position
  objects | get components | where $ is Light and intensity > 2 | select gameObject.name intensity color
  roots | recurse children | where components.count() == 1 | select $path name
  unity.assets("t:Material") | select name shader.name properties["_Color"]
  console | where logType == "Error" | sort sequence desc | first 5 | select message
  scenes | select name path isDirty rootCount
  componentTypes | where name contains "Collider" | select name
  editor | select isPlaying isPaused selection

query.description: RQL query, e.g. objects | where $ is ... | select $ref name

function.name: rql-schema
function.description: Without a type: RQL sources, asset functions, and the component types present in the loaded scenes (with counts), plus GameObject and Transform members. With a type name (e.g. "Light", "Enemy", "Vector3"): that type's members (name type; ro = read-only) and methods. Use it before querying an unfamiliar component.

function.name: screenshot-isolated
function.description:
Renders a screenshot of a target GameObject with configurable isolation, background, camera angle, and lighting. When isolated=true (default), only the target object is visible via layer-based culling and inactive children of the target are temporarily activated for the render (their OnEnable callbacks may fire — restored in finally, but side effects like audio/network/animation events are not undoable). When isolated=false, the existing scene state is rendered as-is without activating inactive objects. Supports custom multi-light setups via JSON. Returns a base64-encoded PNG.

Argument types — give these arguments as RQL values (as in rql-mutate): {key: value, …}, [a, b], "text", 1.5, true, ref("GameObject#12") from a query result, unity.find("Name"); leave out keys you do not need:
GameObjectRef — a GameObject: ref("GameObject#12") from a query, unity.find("Name"), or its name / hierarchy path as text ("Root/Child")

gameObjectRef.description: Reference to the target GameObject (by instanceId, path, or name). RQL: GameObjectRef

includeChildren.description: Include child GameObjects in the render. Default: true.

isolated.description: When true, renders only the target object using layer-based culling. When false, renders the full scene from the computed camera position. Default: true.

backgroundColor.description: Hex background color (e.g. '#404040'). Only used when backgroundMode is SolidColor.

cameraView.description: Camera angle relative to the target object's bounding box. Default: Front.

fieldOfView.description: Camera vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 60.

nearClipPlane.description: Camera near clip plane distance. Default: 0.01.

farClipPlane.description: Camera far clip plane distance. Default: 1000.

padding.description: Framing multiplier around the object. 1.0 = tight fit, 1.5 = 50% extra space. Default: 1.2.

lights.description: JSON array of light configurations. Each object defines type, color, intensity, rotation, position, range, spotAngle, shadows, etc. When null, a default white directional light at rotation (50,-30,0) is used. Example: [{"type":"Directional","color":"#FFF4E5","intensity":1.2,"rotation":[45,-45,0]}]

resolution.description: Output image resolution in pixels (width = height). Default: 512.

function.name: script-execute
function.description:
Compiles and executes C# code dynamically using Roslyn. Supports two modes: full code mode (default) requires a complete class definition, while body-only mode (isMethodBody=true) auto-generates the boilerplate so you only provide the method body. Unity objects (GameObject, Component, etc.) can be passed as parameters using their Ref types (GameObjectRef, ComponentRef, etc.) or directly by type.

Argument types — give these arguments as RQL values (as in rql-mutate): {key: value, …}, [a, b], "text", 1.5, true, ref("GameObject#12") from a query result, unity.find("Name"); leave out keys you do not need:
SerializedMemberList — named values {count: 3, label: "x", target: ref("GameObject#12")}: each is passed as a parameter of the value's type (GameObject, Component, string, int, float, bool)

csharpCode.description: C# code to compile and execute. In full code mode (default, isMethodBody=false): must define a complete class with a static method. Example: 'using UnityEngine; public class Script { public static void Main() { Debug.Log("Hello"); } }'. Do NOT use top-level statements. In body-only mode (isMethodBody=true): provide only the method body statements. The tool auto-generates usings, class, and method header. Example body: 'go.SetActive(false);'. Custom helper classes can still be defined inline in the body-only string after the main logic, but for complex additional class definitions use full code mode instead.

className.description: The name of the class containing the method to execute. In body-only mode this becomes the generated class name.

methodName.description: The name of the method to execute. Must be a static method. In body-only mode this becomes the generated method name.

parameters.description: Values for the method's parameters by name, e.g. {go: ref("GameObject#12"), n: 6}. Leave empty if the method takes none. RQL: SerializedMemberList

isMethodBody.description: When true, 'csharpCode' is treated as just the method body. The tool auto-generates standard using directives (System, UnityEngine, AIGD, com.IvanMurzak.Unity.MCP.Runtime.Extensions, UnityEditor), the class definition, and the method signature (void return type). Parameters from the 'parameters' list are automatically added to the method signature using their typeName and name. When false (default), 'csharpCode' must be a complete C# compilation unit with class and method definitions.

function.name: tests-run
function.description: Execute Unity tests and return detailed results. Supports filtering by test mode, assembly, namespace, class, and method. Recommended to use 'EditMode' for faster iteration during development. Precondition: every open scene MUST be saved (no unsaved changes). If any open scene is dirty, this tool throws an InvalidOperationException listing the dirty scenes; save them and retry.

testMode.description: Test mode to run. Options: 'EditMode', 'PlayMode'. Default: 'EditMode'

testAssembly.description: Specific test assembly name to run (optional). Example: 'Assembly-CSharp-Editor-testable'

testNamespace.description: Specific test namespace to run (optional). Example: 'MyTestNamespace'

testClass.description: Specific test class name to run (optional). Example: 'MyTestClass'

testMethod.description: Specific fully qualified test method to run (optional). Example: 'MyTestNamespace.FixtureName.TestName'

includePassingTests.description: Include details for all tests, both passing and failing (default: false). If you just need details for failing tests, set to false.

includeMessages.description: Include test result messages in the test results (default: true). If you just need pass/fail status, set to false.

includeStacktrace.description: Include stack traces in the test results (default: false).

includeLogs.description: Include console logs in the test results (default: false).

logType.description: Log type filter for console logs. Options: 'Log', 'Warning', 'Assert', 'Error', 'Exception'. (default: 'Warning')

includeLogsStacktrace.description: Include stack traces for console logs in the test results (default: false). This is huge amount of data, use only if really needed.

function.name: unity-tool-list
function.description: List all Unity-MCP tools registered in the connected Unity Editor instance. Optionally filter by regex across tool names, descriptions, and arguments.

regexSearch.description: Regex pattern to filter tools. Matches against tool name, description, and argument names and descriptions.

includeDescription.description: Include tool descriptions in the result. Default: false

includeInputs.description: Include input arguments in the result. Default: None

function.name: submit_answer
function.description: Submit the final answer and end the task.
